subject: Prod impact — FastFin p99 spike + errors: interim mitigation and exec update
body:
From: Paul Roberts <paul.roberts@fastfin.com>
To: priya.natarajan@redwood.ai
Cc: support@fastfin.com
Date: Sat, 27 Nov 2027 20:12:00 -0800
Subject: [ACTION] Sudden p99 spike + 503s for FastFin prod (region: us-west-2)

Hi Priya —

We started seeing user-facing failures around 19:45 PST and sustained high p99 (6–8x normal) and an increase in 503s. Mobile checkout flows are timing out and a subset of requests show queue wait times > 2s before processing. This started right after a marketing campaign push (burst of traffic).

Attached are a sample of traces and the raw request payloads (trace-fastfin-20271127-20.zip, sample-requests-20271127.ndjson). Can you triage? Our CS team is fielding customer calls — we need an ETA and whether this will breach our SLA.

Paul
CTO, FastFin
paul.roberts@fastfin.com

-----
On Sat, 27 Nov 2027 at 20:25 Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai> wrote:

Thanks Paul — I’m escalating to our on-call infra and adding leadership. We’ll set up a short bridge and share mitigations ASAP.

I’ve looped in Rishi (on-call), Vivek (infra), and Laura (ops lead). Priya

Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai

-----
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: priya.natarajan@redwood.ai
Cc: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 27 Nov 2027 20:38:12 -0800
Subject: Re: [ACTION] Sudden p99 spike + 503s for FastFin prod (region: us-west-2)

Quick triage notes (initial):
- Observed patterns in logs: request router queue depth for FastFin pool climbed to concurrency cap and then requests started queuing for ~1.5–2.5s before token generation started.
- Error pattern: increased 502/503 responses correlated with backend KV cache timeouts (KV latency spike) and circuit-breaker trips at the model worker layer.
- Bandwidth: Traffic rate spiked ~3.8x for ~7 minutes following the campaign burst; many requests have longer prompts (median length up ~2.3x).

Immediate actions I’m taking now:
1) Bump FastFin dedicated routing weight and raise concurrency cap for their pool from 64 -> 128 (temporary) to clear queue.
2) Force-disable batch coalescing for FastFin traffic to reduce head-of-line blocking for large prompts.
3) Open temporary bypass to fallback smaller-quantized model (compatible variant) if worker queue exceeds threshold.

I’ll post links to the traces after I collect final traces from the router. ETA for initial reduction in tail: 10–15 minutes after config push.

—Rishi

-----
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: priya.natarajan@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 27 Nov 2027 21:02:45 -0800
Subject: Re: [ACTION] Sudden p99 spike + 503s for FastFin prod (region: us-west-2)

Adding context from infra side:
- Root-cause hypothesis: a bursty upstream campaign sent a high fraction of large-payload requests. The router's default continuous-batching + per-customer concurrency cap produced head-of-line queueing. The increased prompt sizes also stressed KV cache working set causing cache evictions and backend latency that amplified worker-side circuit trips.
- We have telemetry showing the router queue growth aligns with the spike window and worker_utilization peaked.

Mitigations (now):
- Approved Rishi’s concurrency bump and batch-disable for the FastFin pool. We’ll keep the temporary cap increase for 60 minutes and monitor error rate.
- Enabled KV cache read-retry with extended timeout for FastFin requests for the next 30 minutes to avoid premature circuit trips (stopgap).
- Schedule: If tail does not trend down within 30 minutes, we will spin a temporary extra worker pool (same model) in us-west-2 and route a portion of FastFin traffic there. That requires a brief config rollout (5m) and warm-up (3–5m).

Follow-ups for postmortem:
- Evaluate whether default concurrency cap of 64 is safe for bursty workloads with large prompt length; consider making cap heuristics prompt-size aware.
- Revisit batching heuristics to allow weighted priority for customer pools when head-of-line blocking is detected.
- Add an automated early-warning when router queue increases and KV cache miss rate for a single tenant exceed thresholds.

I’ll join the bridge now. Vivek
Head of Infra Engineering

Thanks for the fast response. Two asks from our side:
1) Can you confirm whether this pattern will repeat with our scheduled newsletter blast (same template) tomorrow morning? We need a mitigation plan.
2) FastFin team will request an SLA exception if we have >1% user impact across a 1-hour window. Please advise next steps and a point of contact for credits.

Paul

Subject: Re: [ACTION] Sudden p99 spike + 503s for FastFin prod (region: us-west-2)

Thank you team — and Priya, please keep FastFin's execs updated with the mitigation timeline. A few asks for the exec summary:
- Certify the immediate customer-facing mitigations (what we did, timestamps).
- Short-term plan to prevent recurrence before their newsletter tomorrow (e.g., scheduled capacity bump + traffic shaping during blast, runbook item owners).
- Decision on SLA exception / credits (we need a recommended position to present to finance).

Karthik — please capture the runbook changes and schedule a dry-run for customer blast scenarios in staging. Rishi/Vivek — keep the temporary config and update metrics in the incident channel.

I expect a 1-hour exec summary note with bullet items and proposed credit position. Laura
VP, Customer Ops

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Paul Roberts <paul.roberts@fastfin.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 28 Nov 2027 09:17:00 -0800
Subject: Re: [ACTION] Sudden p99 spike + 503s for FastFin prod (region: us-west-2)

Paul —

Quick customer-facing summary and next steps (ETA: see timestamps below):
- What happened: A marketing-driven burst produced a surge of large-payload requests; router queues hit the per-tenant concurrency cap and head-of-line blocking caused the p99 tail to spike. Secondary effect: KV cache pressure increased backend latency leading to transient 502/503 responses.
- Immediate mitigations (completed):
  * 20:45 UTC (20:53 PST) — Increased tenant concurrency cap 64 -> 128 for FastFin (temporary, 60m window).
  * 20:50 UTC — Disabled batch coalescing for FastFin traffic to reduce HOL blocking.
  * 20:55 UTC — Enabled KV cache extended-read timeout for FastFin to prevent premature circuit-breaker trips.
  * 21:05 UTC — Observed p99 drop to ~1.4x baseline and error rate approaching normal.
- Short-term plan before tomorrow’s blast:
  * Scheduled a controlled capacity bump for their pool during the expected blast window (ops will pre-warm + scale to target).
  * Implement traffic shaping/rate-limiter rule for non-critical endpoints for the blast window.
  * Runbook run-through scheduled with staging traffic at 08:00 PST tomorrow (Karthik owner).
- SLA/credits: We’ve started incident logging and will calculate impact window. Laura recommends we prepare a proposed credit position (reduced invoice for affected window) — we’ll present a recommended amount in the 1-hour exec note.

Attachments: SLA-exception-request.pdf (customer form), traces uploaded to our S3 link.

I’ll update you with the post-incident report and actions.

Best,
Priya
Senior Account Exec, Redwood Inference
priya.natarajan@redwood.ai
